elements.element: Licence extends to Customer's affiliates without written notice or other additional condition.
elements.evidence: Affiliates are included only “on written notice to Kubient,” so the unqualified preferred affiliate coverage is not provided.

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant does not include contractors, and the licence remains without a right of sublicense.
No perpetual duration is stated. The paid-up condition is not demonstrably absent merely because the licence is described as royalty-free.
The licence is expressly described as “revocable,” and there is no exception for paid-up licences.

elements.element: Any subscription licence may be terminated only for an uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no material-breach trigger or cure requirement and instead characterizes the licence generally as revocable. The subscription condition is not demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Transfer is permitted only to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all of Customer's assets, not to successors generally.

elements.element: Licence extends to Customer's affiliates on written notice to Kubient.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly covers “Customer and, on written notice to Kubient, its affiliates.”

elements.element: Licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The non-assignability restriction expressly excepts assignment “to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all of Customer's assets,” covering the specified M&A succession scenarios.

result.reason: The redline implements both fallback requirements and leaves the remainder of the licence grant unchanged. It does not reach the preferred position because affiliate coverage is notice-conditioned, contractors are omitted, the licence remains revocable without perpetual or breach-and-cure protections, and successor transferability is limited to specified M&A events. Drafting quality is reduced by retaining “non-transferable” immediately before an exception only grammatically attached to “non-assignable,” creating avoidable tension over the permitted successor transfer.
